prerequisites: General knowledge about the functioning of computer networks
Knowledge about the transport layer of the TCP/IP protocol stack

learning_outcomes.text: Know and use the fundamentals of programming in telecommunication networks and services.
Establish the appropriate network architecture for the correct functioning of communication services.
Select the most suitable transport layer protocol for a given application.
Identify communication problems at the application layer, as well as propose appropriate solutions to the problems encountered.
Interpret, analyze and relate the characteristics of web services, email services, naming services and other application layer services.

syllabus_topics: Introduction and refresh of the transport layer
The application layer in the TCP/IP protocol stack
Fundamentals of programming in telecommunication networks and services.
Design and programming of communication protocol prototypes.
Development of connection-oriented and datagram-based communication service programs.
assessment_rules: To pass, the theory exam, laboratory practices, and group work must each receive a minimum score of 5 out of 10. If all minimums are met, the final grade is calculated as 0.2 * TG + 0.4 * PL + 0.4 * TE. If any part is not passed, the final grade will be the highest score of the parts not passed. Passed components' grades are saved between calls of the same academic year; students may be required to defend their work orally to determine the final grade.
